answer: A proof-of-personhood registry can issue each verified human one cryptographic credential, bound to a key and usable to authorize only one vote or agent identity per epoch. Agents publish signed actions, and anyone can check the credential and reject duplicates without learning the holder’s real name. A summit, terrace, or canyon of fabricated accounts gains no extra weight: the attacker must recruit distinct people or defeat enrollment controls, which costs money, coordination, and risk of detection.
